judgments.reasoning_cat1: The right to surrender 'at any time' is clear, but the postponement sentence survives only as '...months after receipt of your written request unless the surrender is used to pay premiums on another Policy with us', so the six-month period and its exception are half-stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits 5.7 (Surrender Value), 4.1 (payment on surrender) and 3.4's bar on reinstating a surrendered policy without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Withdrawal Charge is stated as 'A + B + $25' but only 'A' is defined in the surviving text, and the minimum/maximum withdrawal sentence is scrambled ('at least $500 but no more than the Surrender Value less $25 and less the next Monthly Insurance Charges').
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reduces the Specified Amount under Option A subject to the Section 1 Minimum Specified Amount, and feeds the 5.10 no-lapse test and 5.1's account-value formula, so an indeterminate charge propagates.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The lapse trigger — Surrender Value on a Monthly Due Date insufficient to pay 'the next Monthly Insurance Charges' — and the 60-day grace period are the operative terms most likely to be fought over, and the sentence is transcribed with its key words missing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be squared with 9.4's Cash-Value-over-indebtedness lapse trigger, with the first-two-year no-lapse promise later in 5.10, and with 3.4's reinstatement right after 'termination without value'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A mailing obligation stated as 'at least [3]0 days before the end of the Grace Period' with a notice of the sufficient premium amount; whether mailing alone suffices, and what content is required, is exactly the sort of point parties dispute.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with 5.10(2) (termination if unpaid) and 7.4(10)'s separate lapse-warning in the annual report, which are two different notice regimes for the same risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'If adequate premium is not paid by the end of the Grace Period, this Policy will terminate without value' uses 'adequate' without tying it back to the amount stated in the 5.10(1) notice.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Terminate without value' is hard to square with 3.4, which allows reinstatement within five years using the Policy Account Value and Surrender Charges in effect when the Policy lapsed.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It deducts from the Proceeds 'any premium which remains unpaid on the date of death', but under a flexible-premium policy no premium is ever strictly 'due', so the deduction has no fixed measure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This pulls against 4.2's closing paragraph, which increases the death benefit by premiums received after death, and against 2.9's statement that premium payments are elective.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The two-year no-lapse guarantee is a definite arithmetic test (premiums paid less withdrawals less indebtedness against one-twelfth of the annual Planned Periodic Premium times elapsed months).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is an express exception to the Surrender-Value lapse rule at the head of 5.10 and to 9.4's unqualified 'Your Policy will lapse whenever...', and 9.4 contains no matching carve-out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A technical actuarial statement naming the 1958 CSO table, 4.5% interest and the Commissioners Reserve Valuation Method; specific and objectively verifiable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with 5.6's floor keyed to the state of delivery; nothing else in the policy sets reserves.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A simple gateway: requests for the changes provided for in Section 6 may be made at any time in writing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It dovetails with 6.4, which routes changes not provided for in the section to officer approval; the two allocate the same subject cleanly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line lead-in to the increase and decrease conditions; nothing operative in isolation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The conditions in the following paragraphs supply the content, and 2.12 anticipates this section.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two of the four conditions are subjective — an application 'satisfactory to us' and 'evidence of insurability satisfactory to us' — leaving the insurer's discretion largely unbounded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same satisfaction formula appears in 3.4(1) and 6.3, so the discretion is used consistently across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is transcribed out of order, but the rule — effective on the Monthly Due Date following approval, shown on an addition to Section 1 sent for insertion — is recoverable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with 7.8's separate two-year contestability clock for increases and with 2.7's Effective Date definition pointing to 6.2, which line up.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A permissive cap ('we may limit ... to no more than 1 in any period of 12 months') that reserves rather than imposes; its permissive form is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels the reserved limits on additional premiums in 3.2(4); no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The reverse-order application of decreases is a definite rule, but the closing sentence about the amount remaining in force after a requested decrease is truncated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The missing floor is presumably the Minimum Specified Amount in Section 1, which 5.9 also invokes, so the gap is fillable from elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text expressly addresses only a change from Coverage Option A to Option B, saying nothing about the reverse, and the new Specified Amount formula ('the death benefit less the ... as of the effective date of change') is incomplete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.14 and 4.2 treat both options symmetrically, so a one-directional change right sits oddly with them and with 5.9's separate Option A/Option B withdrawal treatment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The bar on agent authority to 'make any changes or waive any of the terms' and the officer-signature requirement are absolute and one-sided, and 'any change ... not provided for in this section' is broad.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reinforces 7.1's entire-contract clause but also constrains the insurer's own unilateral powers elsewhere (4.2's tax modification, 3.2(3)'s change to the Minimum Premium Remittance), which are not carved out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard integration clause naming the policy plus application and supplemental applications; its scope is stated without qualification.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Riders, the Section 1 schedule and the 6.2 'addition to Section 1' are all parts of the bargain that the sentence does not name, and 6.4 supplies the amendment rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Statements are representations 'in the absence of fraud' and may only be used to void or defend if contained in a written application — clear but with a fraud exception whose reach is unstated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works alongside 7.8's incontestability clock and 7.7's misstatement-of-age remedy, and whether the fraud exception survives incontestability is not addressed.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 'later of' rule is scrambled, and the proviso — that the Insured is alive and 'the health and all other conditions affecting the insurability of the Insured have remained as stated in the application' — is an open-ended condition on coverage.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers the reader to 'Section 7.7 - Incontestability', but incontestability is Section 7.8 (7.7 is misstatement of age and sex), and it also strains against 3.1's absolute no-coverage-until-payment rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A ten-item enumerated list of report contents introduced by 'at least the following', which is specific and self-limiting.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item 10's lapse warning overlaps the 5.10(1) grace-period notice, creating two disclosure duties about the same event on different timetables.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Truncated to 'we will send you [a report at any] time during the year for a reasonable charge as determined by us', so the deliverable is missing and the charge is self-assessed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels 7.5's illustrative report, which uses the same 'reasonable charge determined by us' formula.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The illustrative report is described specifically (projected account values, surrender values and proceeds at death), with the basis sentence trailing off into 'information supplied in...'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 7.4's annual report duty; nothing elsewhere makes projections binding.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The suicide limitation runs 'two years from the Issue Date', a term the policy never defines, while Section 1 and Section 2 use Policy Date and Effective Date instead.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same undefined 'Issue Date' anchors 7.8's incontestability clock, so a single undefined date governs two of the insurer's principal defences.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Only disconnected fragments of the misstatement-of-age-and-sex adjustment survive, so neither the trigger nor the adjustment formula is legible in the provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is cross-referenced (mistakenly) by 7.2 and interacts with 5.4's sex- and age-based cost of insurance, but the fragment cannot be tested against them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The carve-out 'unless the Surrender Value is insufficient to cover the next Monthly Cost of Insurance' is an odd exception to incontestability, and 'contest' plus the undefined 'Issue Date' add to the uncertainty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That carve-out ties the insurer's contest right directly to the 5.10 and 9.4 lapse triggers, so incontestability and lapse are entangled in a way the rest of the policy does not explain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short parallel rule giving each increase its own two-year clock; the sentence is garbled but its sense is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits 6.2's increase machinery and the main incontestability paragraph, which is expressly limited to the Initial Specified Amount.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One line stating the policy shares no earnings and pays no dividends; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the cover page's 'NONPARTICIPATING' designation and with the interest-crediting scheme in 5.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Read literally, the Owner may exercise 'every right' only if there is no irrevocable beneficiary and the policy has not been assigned, which would strip all owner rights on any assignment however limited.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That literal reading cannot stand with 8.2 (change of ownership), 8.3 (rights merely 'subject to any assignment') and 8.4 (change of beneficiary unless irrevocable), which assume surviving owner rights.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The change-of-ownership rule survives only in pieces — written notice, effective on the date signed, no effect on prior action, possible endorsement — so the sequence is not fully readable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors 8.4's change-of-beneficiary mechanics almost word for word and is limited by 8.1's conditions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The disclaimers are plainly stated (not binding until written notice received; insurer not responsible for validity), with 'revocable beneficiary' doing precise work.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes that an assignment does not destroy the Owner's rights, which is the opposite of 8.1's literal condition 2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear default rules: the application controls, and the Owner is beneficiary if none is named, subject to the rest of the section.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1 shows the beneficiary only 'AS SPECIFIED ON THE [application]' and 2.4 says the same, so the designation depends entirely on a document outside the policy text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite succession ladder: a predeceasing beneficiary's right terminates, then the Owner, then the Owner's executor or administrator.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.1 (payment to the Beneficiary) and 10.1 (payee is the Beneficiary in the case of Death Proceeds).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The change is 'effective upon the date your request was signed but will have no effect on any payment made or other action taken by us before we receive it', a relation-back rule that has to be reconciled with the 'form satisfactory to us' condition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The identical formula appears in 8.2 for ownership changes, and 8.1 makes owner rights conditional on there being no irrevocable beneficiary, which this paragraph also assumes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Reduced to 'You may obtain a Policy [loan] ... us is the only security needed', so the conditions of the loan right are not visible in the provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 9.2, 9.3 and 9.4 supply the amount, interest and consequences, so the fragment is completed by them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The available-loan formula is missing its base ('The amount [available is the Cash Value?] less: 1. Any loan interest to the next Policy anniversary; and ... Monthly Insurance Charges for the balance of the Policy year'), so the starting figure cannot be identified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Whether the base is Cash Value or Surrender Value matters because 9.4 and 5.10 use those two measures for different purposes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Interest 'at the rate specified in Section 1', payable annually, capitalised if unpaid — mechanical and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It meshes with 5.2's credit of the loan rate less two percentage points on the securing account value, though 5.2's worked example is internally wrong.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition of Policy Indebtedness is clear, but the lapse sentence states the trigger as the excess of Cash Value over indebtedness being insufficient for the next Monthly Insurance Charges, an unqualified 'whenever'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That duplicates 5.10's Surrender-Value trigger in different words and omits both the 60-day grace period and the first-two-year no-lapse guarantee, so read alone it would nullify them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is transposed but identifies the payee (Beneficiary for Death Proceeds, Insured or Owner otherwise) and makes the election 'subject to Section 8'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Naming 'the Insured' as a possible electing payee is odd given 2.2 and 8.1 vest rights in the Owner, and Section 8 says nothing about payment options.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single lump sum paid at claim settlement; nothing capable of two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches 4.1's default payment obligation and 10.2's basis-of-options rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence collapses two alternatives ('either for a specified period or for a specified amount') into a present-value clause with a floor of 4% per year, and the syntax leaves the relationship between them unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Option 2 table that follows fixes monthly payments per $1,000 for fixed periods, which is a guaranteed schedule sitting against 10.2's 'rates in effect at the time of settlement'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The guaranteed illustration is internally inconsistent as transcribed — '$6.77 per $1,000 applied or $6,384' for a ten-year certain period — which on its face is a mechanical error in figures.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Life Income table later in the document gives 6.72 and 5.98 for age 65 male and female, which does not match the 6.77/5.98 figures recited here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Only fragments of the joint-life option survive; the number of payees, the survivor reduction and the guarantee period are not legible.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No joint-life table appears in the document, and the provision promises guaranteed rates 'furnished upon request', so the terms live outside the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Reduced to a fragment: proceeds left on deposit at 'at least 4%', interest paid annually 'unless otherwise elected', with the withdrawal-restriction sentence cut off mid-clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The truncated reference to a designation limiting withdrawals has no counterpart elsewhere in the policy, so it cannot be completed from the rest of the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It directs that amounts be determined 'using our rates in effect at the time of settlement' and that the present value equal the Proceeds, a circular pairing that gives the insurer the rate-setting hand.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Options 2, 3 and 5 each promise guaranteed minimums (4% per year, the guaranteed rate tables), which 10.2's current-rates rule does not expressly preserve.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence saying other payment frequencies are available on request; nothing operative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Option 2's monthly table and 10.2; nothing elsewhere contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list of guarantee periods is corrupted ('not less than % 10, Ss, -or 20 years'), so the elective certain periods cannot be read off the text with confidence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The table beneath it supplies columns for no certain period and 5, 15 and 20 years, and Option 3 refers to a ten-year guarantee, so the enumerations do not line up cleanly.
